reason: Kept, not replaced: xterm.js 6.0.0 is the browser terminal widget (packages/client/ui-sidebar-terminal/src/client/terminal.tsx:3, :102-108). DH-ADR-3 allows a JavaScript island for the terminal, so the same package is vendored as its published ES module and stylesheet and wrapped in one custom element inside a same-origin frame; what changes is the packaging (no bundler, no React wrapper) and that the host emulator answers terminal queries.

Kept with xterm.js: the add-on's proposeDimensions() is the only call used (terminal.tsx:191-200) and it reads xterm.js internals, so version 0.11.0 is vendored beside xterm.js 6.0.0 and upgraded together with it; the island clamps the result to the host limits and sends the resize.

Its one use is timeTicks() for the axis of the experimental Timeline schedule (packages/experimental/timeline/src/client/TimeScale.ts:48). The host renders that view, so round calendar marks are computed in Go with the time package and a fixed ladder of steps in the viewer's time zone.

A Vite build plugin that compiles JSX for the React web client (apps/web/vite.config.ts:6, :174; development dependency only). It exists only because of the upstream JavaScript build: the Go design has no React components and no bundle step (DH-ADR-3).

title: Round calendar tick marks for a time axis: the time package plus a fixed ladder of steps (replaces d3-time)
Templates are html/template behind typed view functions; templ is the verified fallback
htmx 2.0.11 is one vendored file embedded in the binary, with its evaluation features switched off
One Content-Security-Policy: no inline script, no evaluation, no inline style, same-origin manifest; a weaker policy only inside a frame
Live updates are named stream events carrying HTML fragments; a first-party stream script owns the cursor
A browser holds a bounded number of event streams: hidden tabs park
An island is a custom element in an ES module, loaded on demand, with no bundler
Copy, language, time zone and theme are resolved on the host for each request
The browser is the only client: dsh opens it, an optional web app manifest gives it a window, and one attention stream per browser feeds notifications
Every registered view renders its golden file, identically on the page, htmx and stream paths, and writes nothing when it fails
Hostile strings stay inert in every view position; no unchecked conversion to trusted HTML exists
Embedded assets match the manifest and no page names another origin
Every HTML route carries the policy; no template has inline script, handlers or style; htmx settings are locked
Stream writer framing, flushing, handler exit and discarding of a stale live frame
Stream cursor resolution from Last-Event-ID or the after parameter, replay and reset
A slow stream reader is closed and the per-browser stream cap parks the longest-open stream
Every island has a vendored module and a declared policy, and a wider policy is served only in a frame
The launch hands the browser one loopback URL with a one-time token, or prints it when opening is disabled; the dsh binary imports no webview package and builds with cgo off
Chinese and English message tables are complete; language and time zone resolve per request
Rendered pages carry live-region attributes, accessible names and stable ids on focusable swapped elements
The web app manifest is linked and served and no service worker exists; the attention stream carries no transcript content, counts against the stream cap and is never parked
A real browser resumes the event stream after a network cut, a re-created stream and a host restart
Seven tabs over plain HTTP stay usable because hidden tabs park their stream
The Content-Security-Policy holds on real pages with hostile content, including the framed terminal
The dsh command opens the system browser on the same UI, with notifications and an installed window, in each supported browser on Windows, macOS and Linux
Vendored terminal files match the manifest and the terminal frame carries its own policy and attributes
A Go client plays the island's side of the terminal protocol: snapshot, chunks, acknowledgement, input and resize limits
Tick marks fall on round boundaries in three time zones, including across a daylight-saving change
